meta.title: learn-sailing — Learn the parts of a boat
meta.description: An interactive 3D sailboat for learning hull, rig, and orientation terms.

site.name: learn-sailing
site.tagline: Learn the parts of a sailboat

detail.hint: Click a point on the boat or pick a part from the list.

hull.name: Hull
hull.description: The hull is the watertight body of the boat. This first model is a monohull: one hull, not a catamaran.

keel.name: Keel
keel.description: The keel sits under the hull. It provides sideways resistance in the water and counters heeling.

deck.name: Deck
deck.description: The deck is the walking surface on top of the hull. From here you handle halyards, sheets, and the helm.

cockpit.name: Cockpit
cockpit.description: The crew sits in the cockpit aft. Steering and most running rigging are handled from here.

rudder.name: Rudder
rudder.description: The rudder sits at the stern in the water. This boat has a single rudder, not a twin-rudder setup.

tiller.name: Tiller
tiller.description: The tiller is the lever that turns the rudder. Larger yachts often use a wheel instead.

mast.name: Mast
mast.description: The mast stands vertically and carries the sails and standing rigging. A sloop has exactly one mast.

spreaders.name: Spreaders
spreaders.description: Spreaders are cross-arms on the mast. They hold the shrouds out so the mast is better supported sideways.

boom.name: Boom
boom.description: The boom is the horizontal spar at the foot of the mainsail. It holds the sail’s lower edge and is trimmed with the mainsheet.

mainsail.name: Mainsail
mainsail.description: The mainsail sits behind the mast, between mast and boom. It is the sloop’s primary sail.

jib.name: Jib
jib.description: The jib is the headsail in front of the mast. It runs on the forestay and is trimmed with the jib sheets.

forestay.name: Forestay
forestay.description: The forestay is the stay from the masthead to the bow. It supports the mast forward and carries the jib.

backstay.name: Backstay
backstay.description: The backstay runs from the masthead to the stern. It supports the mast aft and is part of the standing rigging.

shrouds.name: Shrouds
shrouds.description: The shrouds support the mast to starboard and port. Together with forestay and backstay they make up the standing rigging.

mainHalyard.name: Main halyard
mainHalyard.description: The main halyard hoists the mainsail up the mast. Halyards are running rigging: you handle them often.

jibHalyard.name: Jib halyard
jibHalyard.description: The jib halyard hoists the jib. It runs to the masthead and is made off on the foredeck or in the cockpit.

mainsheet.name: Mainsheet
mainsheet.description: The mainsheet trims the boom and therefore the mainsail. Sheeting in flattens the sail and brings it closer to the wind.

jibSheet.name: Jib sheet
jibSheet.description: The jib sheets run from the jib clew aft. On each tack you sheet in the leeward sheet.

starboard.name: Starboard
starboard.description: Starboard is the right-hand side when you look forward toward the bow. At night starboard carries a green light.

port.name: Port
port.description: Port is the left-hand side when you look forward toward the bow. At night port carries a red light.

bow.name: Bow
bow.description: The bow is the forward end of the boat. Toward the bow is ahead; the forestay and anchor live here.

stern.name: Stern
stern.description: The stern is the aft end of the boat. Toward the stern is aft; the rudder and often the cockpit sit here.

meta.title: learn-sailing — Sailing simulation
meta.description: Turn the wind and the boat, trim the sails, and see how course and heel go together.

sail.tagline: Learn courses, sail trim, and heel
sail.panelHint: The boat stays put. You rotate wind and heading and trim the sheets.

courses.title: Points of sail
courses.holdHint: Turn the wind and the boat holds the selected point of sail. Sheets stay fine-tunable.
